question: Who among the following are involved in the election of the President of India?1. Elected members of the Lok Sabha2. All members of the Rajya Sabha3. Elected members of the State Assembly4. Elected members of the State Legislative Council (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2, 3 and 4
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1 and 3 only

Explanation:
The election of the President of India involves only the elected members of Lok Sabha and elected members of State Legislative Assemblies. All members of Rajya Sabha (including nominated) and members of State Legislative Councils do not participate in this election. The election is conducted through the single transferable vote system based on the principle of proportional representation. Only elected members can vote in the Presidential election; nominated members of Rajya Sabha and members of Legislative Councils are not entitled to vote. This provision is laid down in Article 54 of the Indian Constitution.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Electors in Presidential election → Elected members of Lok Sabha and State Assemblies
☛ System of Presidential election → Single transferable vote with proportional representation
☛ Constitutional Article → Article 54
☛ Nominated members' right → No vote in Presidential election
☛ State Legislative Council → Not involved in Presidential election
question_hi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति के चुनाव में निम्नलिखित में से कौन शामिल होते हैं?1. लोकसभा के निर्वाचित सदस्य2. राज्यसभा के सभी सदस्य3. राज्य विधानसभा के निर्वाचित सदस्य4. राज्य विधान परिषद के निर्वाचित सदस्य (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 2)

केवल 1 और 3
केवल 1, 2 और 3
1, 2, 3 और 4
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है केवल 1 और 3

Explanation:
भारत के राष्ट्रपति के चुनाव में लोकसभा के निर्वाचित सदस्य और राज्य विधानसभा के निर्वाचित सदस्य शामिल होते हैं। राज्यसभा के सभी सदस्य (मनोनीत सहित) और राज्य विधान परिषद के सदस्य इस चुनाव में भाग नहीं लेते। यह चुनाव एकल संक्रमणीय मत प्रणाली द्वारा आनुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व के सिद्धांत पर होता है। राष्ट्रपति के चुनाव में केवल निर्वाचित सदस्य ही मतदान कर सकते हैं, जबकि राज्यसभा के मनोनीत सदस्य और विधान परिषद के सदस्यों को मतदान का अधिकार नहीं है। यह प्रावधान भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 54 में दिया गया है।

question: When was a member of the British Cabinet appointed as a 'Secretary of State for India' and made responsible for all matters related to the governance of India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: 1919
1911
1929
1858
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1858

Explanation:
In 1858, a member of the British Cabinet was appointed as the Secretary of State for India. This was part of the reorganization of British rule in India. The Government of India Act 1858 ended the rule of the East India Company and established direct rule by the British Crown. The Secretary of State was made responsible for all matters related to the governance of India and was accountable to the British Parliament. The Governor-General was given the title of Viceroy. Lord Canning became the first Viceroy of India. This system continued until 1947.

☛ East India Company rule ended → Transferred to British Crown in 1858
☛ First Viceroy of India → Lord Canning (1858-1862)
☛ Role of Secretary of State → Supervise all matters related to the governance of India

question: In a federal country, disputes regarding federal matters are resolved by which of the following? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: High Courts
Lower courts
Supreme Court
Union Government
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Supreme Court

Explanation:
In a federal country, disputes regarding federal matters are resolved by the Supreme Court. It acts as the guardian and final interpreter of the constitution. In a federal system, powers are divided between the center and states, and the Supreme Court has the authority to resolve disputes arising from this division. In India, under Article 131, the Supreme Court has original jurisdiction to hear disputes between the Union and states or between states. This court ensures the supremacy of the constitution and protects the federal structure.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Which jurisdiction of the Supreme Court deals with federal disputes? → Original jurisdiction
☛ Who is the guardian of the constitution in a federal country? → Supreme Court
☛ Who gives the final decision in center-state disputes? → Supreme Court
☛ On what basis is the division of powers in a federal system? → Constitution

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides that 'It shall be the duty of the Union and the State Public Service Commissions to conduct examinations for appointments to the services of the Union and the services of the State, respectively'? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Article 319
Article 318
Article 320
Article 322
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 320

Explanation:
Article 320 of the Indian Constitution defines the duties of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (SPSCs). It states that it shall be the duty of these commissions to conduct examinations for appointments to the services of the Union and the State, respectively. Additionally, Article 320 provides for advising on recruitment processes, promotions, transfers, and disciplinary matters. This article is crucial for ensuring transparency and merit in public services. Article 319 deals with conditions of service of members, Article 318 with appointment and service conditions, and Article 322 with expenses of the commissions.

question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution facilitates people to move freely throughout the territory of India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Article 19(1)(b)
Article (19)(1)(d)
Article 19(1)(a)
Article (19)(1)(c)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 19(1)(d)

Explanation:
Article 19(1)(d) of the Indian Constitution grants citizens the right to move freely throughout the territory of India. This fundamental right is one of the six freedoms under Article 19, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the state. Article 19(1)(a) deals with freedom of speech and expression, (b) with the right to assemble peacefully, and (c) with the right to form associations. Thus, the right to free movement is specifically protected under Article 19(1)(d).

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा अनुच्छेद लोगों को भारत के पूरे क्षेत्र में स्वतंत्र रूप से घूमने की सुविधा प्रदान करता है? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 19(1)(b)
अनुच्छेद (19)(1)(d)
अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a)
अनुच्छेद (19)(1)(c)
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 19(1)(d)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 19(1)(d) नागरिकों को भारत के पूरे क्षेत्र में स्वतंत्र रूप से घूमने का अधिकार प्रदान करता है। यह मौलिक अधिकार छह स्वतंत्रताओं में से एक है, जिसे राज्य द्वारा उचित प्रतिबंधों के अधीन किया जा सकता है। अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a) अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता, (b) शांतिपूर्वक एकत्र होने की स्वतंत्रता, (c) संघ बनाने की स्वतंत्रता से संबंधित है। इस प्रकार, स्वतंत्र आवागमन का अधिकार अनुच्छेद 19(1)(d) के तहत संरक्षित है।

question: Under which part of the Indian Constitution are the Fundamental Duties placed? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Part III
Part IVA
Part I
Part IV
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part IVA

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties are enshrined in Part IVA of the Indian Constitution. This part was added by the 42nd Amendment Act (1976) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. Article 51A in this part lists 11 fundamental duties for citizens, such as respecting the national flag and the Constitution, following the ideals of the freedom struggle, and protecting the environment. These duties are moral and legal obligations but are not enforceable by courts. Part III deals with Fundamental Rights, Part I with the Union and its territory, and Part IV with Directive Principles of State Policy.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Under which part are Fundamental Duties placed? → Part IVA (Article 51A)
☛ Which amendment added them? → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ How many Fundamental Duties are there? → 11
☛ Which committee recommended them? → Swaran Singh Committee
☛ Are Fundamental Duties enforceable by courts? → No
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के किस भाग में मौलिक कर्तव्य रखे गए हैं? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options_hi: भाग III
भाग IVA
भाग I
भाग IV
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भाग IVA

question: Which of the following cases established the Right to Privacy as a fundamental right in the Constitution of India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Minerva Mills Ltd. vs Union Of India
Golaknath vs State Of Punjab
SR Bommai vs Union of India
Justice KS Puttaswamy (Retd) vs the Union of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Justice KS Puttaswamy (Retd) vs the Union of India

Explanation:
The Supreme Court in Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) vs Union of India case on 24 August 2017 declared the Right to Privacy as a fundamental right under Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty). A 9-judge Constitution bench unanimously ruled that privacy is protected under Part III of the Constitution. This judgment overruled previous decisions (like M.P. Sharma vs Satish Chandra and Kharak Singh vs State of U.P.) where privacy was not considered a fundamental right. The case arose from petitions challenging the Aadhaar scheme and privacy violations. The court held that privacy is intrinsic to life and dignity.

question: What provision of the Indian Constitution guarantees the independence of the judiciary? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Directive Principles of State Policy
Fundamental Rights
Preamble
Judicial Review
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Judicial Review

Explanation:
The provision of the Indian Constitution that guarantees the independence of the judiciary is Judicial Review. It empowers the Supreme Court and High Courts to examine the constitutionality of laws and executive actions. Through judicial review, courts can declare any law unconstitutional if it violates the basic structure of the Constitution. This power is embodied in Articles 13, 32, 131-136, 143, 226, 227, etc. Judicial review enables the judiciary to act as a check on the legislature and executive, ensuring the supremacy of the Constitution and judicial independence. Other options like Directive Principles, Fundamental Rights, and Preamble do not directly guarantee judicial independence.

question: Which of the following is NOT a role played by NITI Aayog in the localisation of SDGs in India? (RRB Technician Grade III (29/12/2024) Shift 1)

Benchmarking states based on SDG performance metrics
Serving as a platform for collaboration among states
solution:

Explanation:
NITI Aayog plays a significant role in the localisation of SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals) in India, but preparing the National Indicator Framework (NIF) is not its role. These activities support SDG localisation. Thus, preparing the NIF is not a function of NITI Aayog.

question: The President has the power to dissolve which house of Parliament?  (RRB JE ECE (22/04/2025) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: Lok Sabha only
Legislative Assembly
Both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha
Rajya Sabha only
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lok Sabha only

Explanation:
The President of India has the power to dissolve the Lok Sabha (House of the People). This power is granted under Article 85(2)(b) of the Indian Constitution. The Lok Sabha has a term of 5 years, but the President can dissolve it before the expiry of its term. Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved; one-third of its members retire every two years. On dissolution, the President, on the advice of the Prime Minister, orders fresh elections. This power is a key feature of the parliamentary democracy in India.

question: The power to issue an ordinance when Parliament is NOT in session is given to the President under which Article? (RRB JE ECE (22/04/2025) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: Article 72
Article 110
Article 123
Article 356
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 123

Explanation:
Article 123 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session. This power is similar to Article 213 which allows the Governor to issue ordinances during the recess of the state legislature. An ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament. However, it must be approved by Parliament within 6 weeks of reassembly; otherwise, it ceases to operate. It is important to note that an ordinance can only be issued when the President is satisfied that immediate action is necessary. Article 72 deals with the power of pardon, Article 110 defines money bills, and Article 356 relates to President's rule.

question: Dr. BR Ambedkar described which part of the Indian Constitution as its ‘novel features', while Granville Austin referred to it as the ‘Conscience of the Constitution’? (RRB JE CE (22/04/2025) Shift 2 CBT 2)

Fundamental Duties
Directive Principles of State Policy

Explanation:

These principles direct the state to frame policies and enact laws, but are non-justiciable. On the other hand, renowned constitutional expert Granville Austin called them the 'Conscience of the Constitution', because they reflect the socio-economic objectives of the Constitution. These principles are inspired by the Irish Constitution and aim to establish a welfare state. They act as a guide for the government and are fundamental in the governance of the country.

question: Which Article provides Ministers the right to participate in parliamentary proceedings but without voting rights? (RRB JE CE (22/04/2025) Shift 2 CBT 2)

Article 88

solution:

Under this article, ministers can take part in debates, defend policies, and answer questions, but cannot vote on any matter. This ensures coordination between the executive and legislature in a parliamentary democracy.

question: Which Indian Constitutional Amendment Act has NOT amended anything in the Directive Principles of the State Policy? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: 86th Amendment Act
48th Amendment Act
42nd Amendment Act
97th Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 48th Amendment Act

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution. The 42nd Amendment (1976) made several changes to the DPSP, adding Article 39A (equal justice), Article 43A (participation in industry management), and Article 48A (environment protection). The 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 21A (right to education), converting a DPSP into a fundamental right, and amended Article 45. The 97th Amendment (2011) added Article 43B (promotion of cooperative societies). The 48th Amendment Act (1984) primarily amended Article 356 (President's Rule) provisions and did not make any changes to the DPSP articles.

question: Which organisation does the Ministry of Rural Development cooperate with for rural development in Asia and the Pacific? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Asian Development Bank (ADB)
World Bank
Centre on Integrated Rural Development for Asia and Pacific (CIRDAP)
African-Asian Rural Development Organization (AARDO)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Centre on Integrated Rural Development for Asia and Pacific (CIRDAP)

Explanation:
The Ministry of Rural Development cooperates with CIRDAP for rural development in Asia and the Pacific. CIRDAP is an intergovernmental organisation established in 1979. Its member countries include India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar, China, Iran, and Malaysia. The headquarters of CIRDAP is located in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The organisation provides research, training, and policy support in the field of rural development. Through CIRDAP, the Government of India shares experiences and best practices in rural development with other countries in the Asia-Pacific region. The Asian Development Bank (ADB) and World Bank are financial institutions, while AARDO deals with African-Asian rural development.

question: Which authority decides citizenship for people in newly added territories? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Union Government
Election Commission
Supreme Court
State Government
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Union Government

Explanation:
According to the Indian Constitution, the authority to decide citizenship for people in newly added territories rests with the Union Government (Central Government). This power is vested in the Parliament, which acts through the Union Government. Under Article 7 of the Constitution and the Citizenship Act, 1955, the Union Government has the authority to grant or deny citizenship to residents of territories that are annexed or acquired. The Election Commission deals with election conduct, the Supreme Court performs judicial review, and the State Government does not have the power to decide citizenship. Thus, the Union Government is the supreme authority in this matter.

question: What is the primary role of the Gram Panchayat in the Panchayati Raj System in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: To manage urban infrastructure
To conduct provincial elections, helping the Election Commission
To act as the judicial forum for local disputes
To serve as the executive body of village self-government
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To serve as the executive body of village self-government

Explanation:
The Gram Panchayat is the lowest tier in the Panchayati Raj system in India and acts as the executive body of village self-government. It is responsible for the development and administration of the village, including basic amenities like roads, water supply, sanitation, education, and health. The Gram Panchayat is elected by adult villagers and headed by a Sarpanch. It is accountable to the Gram Sabha. Urban infrastructure is managed by municipalities, provincial elections are conducted by the State Election Commission, and local disputes are adjudicated by Gram Nyayalayas. Thus, the primary role of the Gram Panchayat is to serve as the executive body of village self-government.

question: Which languages were added to the Eighth Schedule by the 71st Amendment Act, 1992? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Sindhi, Tamil and Urdu
Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali
Kannada, Telugu and Marathi
Bodo, Santhali and Maithili
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali

Explanation:
The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution originally included 14 languages. The 71st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali, increasing the total number of languages to 18. This amendment was made to recognize linguistic diversity. Konkani is spoken in Goa and Karnataka, Manipuri is the main language of Manipur, and Nepali is spoken in Sikkim and West Bengal. Later, the 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Santhali, Maithili and Dogri.

question: In the ministerial hierarchy in India, Ministers of State generally have: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: authority over the Cabinet portfolios
. no executive responsibility in any of the portfolios
secondary rank within the portfolios assigned to Cabinet Ministers
equal standing with Cabinet Ministers in their assigned portfolios
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is secondary rank within the portfolios assigned to Cabinet Ministers

Explanation:
In India's Council of Ministers, Ministers of State (MoS) work under Cabinet Ministers. They do not hold independent charge but assist in the departments assigned to Cabinet Ministers. Their rank is secondary to Cabinet Ministers, and they are given subordinate responsibilities in departmental work. According to Article 74 of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is headed by the Prime Minister. Cabinet Ministers play a key role in policy-making, while Ministers of State assist in implementation under their guidance.

☛ When is a Minister of State given independent charge? → When they are assigned separate departments
☛ What is the main difference between a Cabinet Minister and a Minister of State? → Cabinet Ministers attend Cabinet meetings, Ministers of State do not
☛ How is the size of the Council of Ministers determined in India? → It depends on the discretion of the Prime Minister

question: Which agreement is linked to the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1985? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Shimla Agreement
Indo-Sri Lanka Pact
Assam Accord
Kashmir Agreement
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Assam Accord

Explanation:
The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1985 was introduced as a result of the Assam Accord. This accord was signed in 1985 between the Government of India and leaders of the Assam Movement to address the issue of illegal immigrants in Assam. The Act granted citizenship to foreign nationals who entered Assam between 1966 and 1971. It relaxed the eligibility criteria for citizenship specifically for the state of Assam. The Assam Accord aimed to identify and deport illegal immigrants who entered after 1971. Other options are incorrect: Shimla Agreement is between India and Pakistan, Indo-Sri Lanka Pact is related to Tamil issues, and Kashmir Agreement pertains to Jammu and Kashmir. Thus, the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1985 is directly linked to the Assam Accord.

☛ Between whom was the Assam Accord signed? → Government of India and leaders of Assam Movement
☛ What was the objective of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1985? → To identify and deport illegal immigrants in Assam
question_hi: नागरिकता (संशोधन) अधिनियम 1985 किस समझौते से सम्बंधित है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: शिमला समझौता
भारत-श्रीलंका समझौता
असम समझौता
कश्मीर समझौता
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है असम समझौता

Explanation:
नागरिकता (संशोधन) अधिनियम 1985, असम समझौते (Assam Accord) के तहत लाया गया था। यह समझौता 1985 में भारत सरकार और असम आंदोलन के नेताओं के बीच हस्ताक्षरित हुआ था, जिसका उद्देश्य असम में अवैध प्रवासियों की पहचान और निर्वासन था। इस अधिनियम ने उन विदेशी नागरिकों को नागरिकता प्रदान की जो 1966 से 1971 के बीच असम में आए थे। इसके तहत नागरिकता के पात्रता मापदंडों में ढील दी गई। यह अधिनियम विशेष रूप से असम राज्य से संबंधित है और अवैध प्रवासन की समस्या को हल करने के लिए बनाया गया था। शिमला समझौता भारत-पाकिस्तान के बीच है, भारत-श्रीलंका समझौता तमिल मुद्दों से जुड़ा है, और कश्मीर समझौता कश्मीर से संबंधित है।
